criteria.requirement: Closed evidence record; the test-only unit-distribution profile never qualifies a production backend
Datastore on AF_UNIX only, one member, no peers
Apiserver binds a loopback address

No anonymous, static-token, bootstrap-token, front-proxy request-header or external (JWT, webhook) authentication; no cluster-admin credential, cluster or front-proxy CA key or bootstrap token on the host; service-account signing key readable by the apiserver only
Authorization exactly Node then RBAC from a sealed structured configuration file (the binary default without flags is AlwaysAllow; the file is reloaded on change)

Required admission plugins enabled (NodeRestriction is off by default upstream); webhook admission, MutatingAdmissionPolicy, NamespaceAutoProvision, ImagePolicyWebhook and AlwaysAdmit disabled; nothing outside the allowed set
Per-controller credentials (upstream default off); only inventory controllers; every required-disabled controller off; no signing key in the controller-manager
Kubelet: no certificate rotation or TLS bootstrap, no static pods, no anonymous or read-only access, Webhook authorization
Exactly the implementation profile's components, each a separate process from a distinct executable in its W02a confined type
Only local APIServices and no CustomResourceDefinitions
No automounted tokens; every in-cluster API client is a closure identity without policy-relevant grants
Container runtime socket reachable only from the kubelet's confined type
All control-plane configuration sealed, including component definitions and admission manifests when used (reloaded on change); auto-apply manifest directories empty and sealed
Pinned, offline, license-allowed artifacts with no runtime downloads or auto-update
Kubernetes release within the v1.37 baseline this inventory was derived from (no pre-releases)
Feature gates keep their v1.37 defaults

Closure derivation: upstream identities hold exactly their bootstrap-derived grants; full authority only for system:masters and system:apiserver; required-disabled controller accounts excluded; closure service accounts only in kube-system
Every subject holding a policy write, status write, identity-acquisition or escalation verb, or a workload grant at cluster scope or in kube-system is a closure identity
Closure identities with grants exist; bindings of controller accounts that do not exist are dormant
No grant beyond the subject's closure entry
The policy writer's escalate and bind only on the named planeon Roles
Required closure identities present
An apiserver restart during ACTIVE invalidates the generation: bootstrap-roles and the system-namespace and authentication-info controllers write policy kinds at start
Policy-kind objects carry no ownerReferences, so the wildcard garbage collector cannot delete them; observer-checked
No ClusterRole with an aggregationRule is bound in the qualification namespace (the aggregation controller is disabled, so such roles keep stale rules)
API Priority and Fairness objects affect availability only; system:masters is exempt; only the in-process producer writes them
No Secret of type kubernetes.io/service-account-token and no bootstrap-token Secret exists; Secret reads then yield no credential; observer-checked
No ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, MutatingWebhookConfiguration or MutatingAdmissionPolicy(Binding) object exists, although their admission plugins are disabled (spec P6); observer-checked

Recommendation for W02f: hold the A2 admission policies in sealed file-based admission manifests (ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig, beta and default on in v1.37), because API-registered policies cannot guard admission objects
